tweets.title: India has once again rejected China’s objections over Arunachal Pradesh, with MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal reiterating that the state is an “inalienable and integral part of India” and that nothing can change this reality. The statement comes after India formally identified 27 locations in Arunachal Pradesh by their standard names on the official Survey of India map, including strategically and historically significant places such as Long Ju, Thag La, Jairampur and Jaswant Garh. Beijing’s attempts to assign Chinese names to locations in Arunachal Pradesh cannot alter India’s sovereignty or the ground reality. India has also reiterated that peace and tranquillity along the LAC remain essential for the broader India-China relationship.
tweets.content:
India has once again rejected China’s objections over Arunachal Pradesh, with MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal reiterating that the state is an “inalienable and integral part of India” and that nothing can change this reality.

The statement comes after India formally identified 27 locations in Arunachal Pradesh by their standard names on the official Survey of India map, including strategically and historically significant places such as Long Ju, Thag La, Jairampur and Jaswant Garh.

Beijing’s attempts to assign Chinese names to locations in Arunachal Pradesh cannot alter India’s sovereignty or the ground reality.

India has also reiterated that peace and tranquillity along the LAC remain essential for the broader India-China relationship.

tweets.title: GRSE has launched ‘Shruti’, the Indian Navy’s second Next Generation Offshore Patrol Vessel (NGOPV), in Kolkata. With around 85% indigenous, Shruti is part of GRSE’s contribution to the Navy’s wider 11-ship NGOPV programme. At ~3,000 tonnes and 113m long, the vessel can reach 23 knots and has an endurance of 8,500 nautical miles at 14 knots. It is designed for maritime surveillance, interdiction, anti-piracy, special operations, mine warfare, counter-infiltration, HADR and search & rescue.
tweets.content:
GRSE has launched ‘Shruti’, the Indian Navy’s second Next Generation Offshore Patrol Vessel (NGOPV), in Kolkata.

With around 85% indigenous, Shruti is part of GRSE’s contribution to the Navy’s wider 11-ship NGOPV programme.

At ~3,000 tonnes and 113m long, the vessel can reach 23 knots and has an endurance of 8,500 nautical miles at 14 knots. It is designed for maritime surveillance, interdiction, anti-piracy, special operations, mine warfare, counter-infiltration, HADR and search & rescue.

tweets.title: R to @sidhant: MEA on India, China border situation "In matters relating to the border areas between India and China, we have always emphasised in discussions with the Chinese side that we consider these issues as most serious and that the maintenance of peace and tranquility in these areas is of the utmost importance. We have also stated that the state of the border affairs will reflect on the state of our larger bilateral ties. This was also reiterated at the recently held 36th Meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on India-China border affairs ( WMCC) on 6th Aug 2026. At this meeting, the two sides engaged in frank discussions and reviewed the situation along the Line of Actual Control (LAC). The Indian side again underlined that maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas is essential for the overall development of bilateral relations. It was agreed to continue to use existing diplomatic and military channels, including the WMCC, local commander‑level meetings and other agreed mechanisms, to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC."

tweets.title: SAUDI–TURKEY–PAKISTAN DEFENCE PACT FACES ITS FIRST TEST Just 48 hours after Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a pact declaring an attack on one as an attack on all three, a Houthi drone struck an Aramco refinery in Jizan. Saudi Arabia confirmed the resulting fire was extinguished. Yet neither Turkey nor Pakistan publicly responded or intervened. The pact promises collective deterrence, but its actual military obligations remain unclear. Turkey’s foreign minister has said members would first consult on the nature and scale of assistance. The real test may come if a member faces a significantly larger attack, and whether the others would actually be willing to fight.
tweets.content:
SAUDI–TURKEY–PAKISTAN DEFENCE PACT FACES ITS FIRST TEST

Just 48 hours after Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a pact declaring an attack on one as an attack on all three, a Houthi drone struck an Aramco refinery in Jizan.

Saudi Arabia confirmed the resulting fire was extinguished. Yet neither Turkey nor Pakistan publicly responded or intervened.

The pact promises collective deterrence, but its actual military obligations remain unclear. Turkey’s foreign minister has said members would first consult on the nature and scale of assistance.

The real test may come if a member faces a significantly larger attack, and whether the others would actually be willing to fight.

tweets.title: CENTRAL GOVERNMENT TURNS FOCUS TO J&K DEMOGRAPHIC CHANGES A four-member Central Committee on Demographic Change, headed by retired Justice Prakash Prabhakar Navlekar, has arrived in Jammu & Kashmir for a three-day assessment of alleged demographic shifts and their security implications. Officials estimate around 13,700 undocumented Rohingya/Bangladeshi migrants across Jammu, Samba and Kathua, although there are no official figures. The panel will examine border areas and localities in Jammu division where undocumented settlements have been reported, review existing verification mechanisms and recommend systems for identification. There is heightened scrutiny of illegal immigration and concerns over its potential demographic and security implications in sensitive border districts by the government.
